events.title: Pope Urban II Calls for the First Crusade
events.description: On the final day of the Council of Clermont in France, Pope Urban II delivered a sermon urging Western Christians to take up arms and aid the Byzantine Empire against Seljuk Turk advances, and to reclaim Jerusalem. The crowd reportedly responded with cries of 'Deus vult' (God wills it).
events.significance: This speech launched the First Crusade, beginning centuries of religiously motivated military campaigns that profoundly shaped relations between Europe, the Byzantine world, and the Middle East.

events.title: Scuttling of the French Fleet at Toulon
events.description: As German forces moved to seize the French naval base at Toulon during Operation Lila, French commanders ordered their ships scuttled. Roughly 77 vessels, including battleships, cruisers, and submarines, were sunk or destroyed by their own crews.
events.significance: The act denied the Axis powers access to a substantial part of the French navy and marked the end of the Vichy regime's limited autonomous military force.

events.title: Assassination of Harvey Milk and George Moscone
events.description: San Francisco Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk, one of the first openly gay elected officials in the United States, were shot and killed at City Hall by former supervisor Dan White.
events.significance: The killings shocked the nation, and Milk became a lasting symbol and martyr of the LGBTQ rights movement, with his legacy inspiring political activism for decades.

events.title: Alfred Nobel Signs His Last Will
events.description: At the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite, signed his final will, leaving the bulk of his fortune to establish prizes honoring achievements in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace.
events.significance: The will led to the creation of the Nobel Prizes, first awarded in 1901, which became among the most prestigious international honors in the world.
